h1: The 6 Best Humidifiers Under $150 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 humidifiers under $150 compared on tank size, mist output, auto mode and cleaning ease, from top-fill Levoits to big tanks.
summary: The Levoit Classic300S Smart is the best humidifier under $150: top-fill design, auto mode and app control in the $50 to $100 bracket. The Levoit Large Room with a 6.2 L tank and 320 ml/h output is the choice for a big bedroom. The Levoit Classic300 stretches a fill to 60 hours, and the Levoit Top Fill is the cheapest to own.
intro: Most people pick a humidifier by tank size, then find they are refilling it at dawn or scrubbing a narrow-necked tank every weekend. The real cost of a humidifier is maintenance. A model you dread cleaning gets cleaned rarely, and a tank with a film of residue puts more into the air than moisture. Top-fill designs and wide openings exist for that reason.

This ranking sorted six humidifiers priced below $150 by how easy they are to run daily: fill method, runtime, auto humidity control and cleaning access. Output matters too, but a unit that runs only when you tolerate its upkeep outperforms a more powerful one that sits empty. Every model here sits in the $25 to $100 range, well under the cap.

products.name: Levoit Classic300S Ultrasonic Smart Top Fill Humidifier
products.verdict: Smart top-fill ultrasonic model with auto mode and a claimed 4x faster humidification.
products.description:
The Classic300S is a smart upgrade on the plain Classic300: an ultrasonic mist, a top-fill opening and an auto mode that holds humidity without you adjusting a knob. The listing claims 4x faster humidification than a basic unit, and the smart control lets you manage it from your phone, which helps when the unit sits across a bedroom.

It ranks first because it removes the two daily chores, refilling and fiddling, while staying in the $50 to $100 bracket. Against the Classic300, you pay for auto mode and app control, which matter if humidity swings overnight. Against the Large Room Levoit, you give up tank size but get smarter operation.

Best for bedrooms where you want steady humidity without checking. The caveat is that app features rely on home Wi-Fi, and the listing does not publish a tank size.
products.idealFor: Bedroom users who want steady humidity without manual adjustment.
products.skipIf: You want the cheapest possible humidifier.

products.name: Levoit Humidifiers for Bedroom Large Room
products.verdict: A 6.2 L tank and 320 ml/h mist output, with microbial-resistant material and precise auto mode.
products.description:
This Levoit is the volume pick: a 6.2 L tank paired with 320 ml/h of mist output, a pairing designed to humidify a bigger room quickly. The tank is made of microbial-resistant material, which slows the slimy film that forms in standing water, and a precise auto mode manages the output for you.

It ranks second because its listing is thinner on features than the Classic300S, with no smart control mentioned. Against the Hiswelle, which shares the large-room label, the Levoit publishes real numbers, and 320 ml/h output is a clear spec to compare. It lands in the $50 to $100 bucket.

Best for a main bedroom or living area. The caveat is that a 6.2 L tank is heavy to carry when full, so fill it in place where you can.
products.idealFor: Larger bedrooms that need more mist output and a big tank.
products.skipIf: You want app control or a small footprint.

products.name: Levoit Classic300 Ultrasonic Top Fill Humidifier
products.verdict: 60 hours of listed runtime, a 1-step top refill, and a knob with a 360 degree nozzle.
products.description:
The Classic300 is the manual version of the Classic300S. It lists 60 hours of runtime, which means less frequent refilling, a one-step top refill and a simple knob control with a 360 degree nozzle for aiming the mist. The top-fill opening is also the reason cleaning is quick.

It ranks third because it lacks auto mode and smart features, so you have to set the knob yourself and watch the room. That is fine for people who like a dial. Against the Levoit Top Fill below, it publishes its runtime, and against the Classic300S it saves money at the same $50 to $100 bucket.

Best for anyone who wants a simple, long-running humidifier. The caveat is that without auto mode, it can over-humidify a small room if you leave it on high.
products.idealFor: People who want a simple humidifier with fewer refills.
products.skipIf: You want the unit to manage humidity for you.

products.name: Levoit Top Fill Humidifiers for Bedroom
products.verdict: Fast humidification all night, a top-fill design and easier cleaning, at $25 to $50.
products.description:
The cheapest Levoit in the group is a top-fill bedroom humidifier built for fast humidification through the night, and the listing highlights that it is much easier to clean. In the $25 to $50 bracket, it costs about half as much as the other Levoits here.

It ranks fourth because the specs are the lightest. There is no tank size, no mist rate and no auto mode in the listing, so you cannot judge how it compares with the 320 ml/h Large Room model. What it provides is the brand's easy-fill design at the lowest price, which suits a first humidifier.

Best for a small bedroom on a budget. The caveat is that the missing numbers leave you guessing about room coverage, so keep it to a modest-sized room.
products.idealFor: A first humidifier for a modest bedroom.
products.skipIf: You need to cover a large room.

products.name: Humidifiers for Bedroom Large Room
products.verdict: Cool mist with aromatherapy, ambient lighting and auto shut-off when the tank is empty.
products.description:
This unit, which the listing attributes to Hiswelle, is a cool mist humidifier for large rooms with extras: aromatherapy, ambient lighting and an auto shut-off function that stops it when the tank runs dry. Auto shut-off protects the unit from running empty, which matters if you fall asleep before it finishes.

It ranks fifth because the extras are not core humidifier performance, and the listing offers no tank size or output figure to back the large-room claim. Against the Levoit Large Room, which publishes 6.2 L and 320 ml/h, this one asks for more trust. The same $50 to $100 bracket applies.

Best for people who like aromatherapy and a soft glow. The caveat is that aroma use can leave residue in the tank, so clean it more often.
products.idealFor: Bedroom users who want a soft light and scent with their humidifier.
products.skipIf: You care about published tank and mist numbers.

products.name: Everlasting Comfort 6L Large Humidifier for Bedroom
products.verdict: A 6 L tank, a filterless design that is easy to clean and 360 degree coverage, at $25 to $50.
products.description:
Everlasting Comfort offers a 6 L tank at the lowest price tier alongside the top-fill Levoit, with a filterless design that is easy to clean and mist coverage described as 360 degrees. A 6 L reservoir means fewer refills than the smaller Levoits, and filterless means no replacement cartridges to buy.

It ranks last because the listing has no auto mode, runtime or output figure, and the fill method is not described. Against the 6.2 L Levoit, it matches the capacity at a lower $25 to $50 bracket but gives up the published 320 ml/h and microbial-resistant tank. It is the value pick for bigger tanks.

Best for budget buyers who want a big tank. The caveat is that, without published output, you will not know how large a room it truly handles.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want a large tank and no filters to replace.
products.skipIf: You want smart control or published output.

whatMatters.detail: Top-fill humidifiers let you pour water in without lifting the tank off the base, and the wide opening makes scrubbing easy. Check the listing for a top-fill or wide opening. A narrow-necked tank is the commonest reason owners stop cleaning, which lets biofilm build up. Reach into the tank with your hand before buying, or study the listing photos, to confirm you can wipe every corner.

A 6.2 L tank, as on the Levoit Large Room, runs far longer than a small one, but weighs about 14 pounds when full. Compare the listed runtime, such as the Classic300's 60 hours, with your refill habits. Runtime depends on mist setting, so lower settings stretch it. Treat any runtime figure as a best case at the lowest mist setting, and divide the tank volume by the output rate to estimate your own hours.

Milliliters per hour tells you how much water enters the air. The Levoit Large Room lists 320 ml/h. Bigger rooms need more output, and units without a published figure are guesses. Match output to room size, and prefer listings that give a number. A bedroom of average size is well served by a few hundred ml/h, while an open living area needs far more output to register on a hygrometer.

Auto mode uses a built-in sensor to hold a target humidity. Without it, a humidifier can push a small room above 60 percent, which encourages mold. The Classic300S and Levoit Large Room list auto mode. Check that the listing names a humidity sensor, not only a timer. A cheap hygrometer on the nightstand is a useful check, because built-in sensors sit close to the unit and can read higher than the room.

Mineral scale and slime build up in any tank. Microbial-resistant plastic slows the slime, and filterless designs avoid replacing cartridges. Check the listing for cleaning claims, and plan on weekly rinses and a vinegar descale regardless of the model. Hard water leaves white dust on furniture, so use distilled or filtered water if the listing says nothing about a demineralizing cartridge.

faq.q: Does a humidifier under $150 work for a large room?
faq.a: Yes, if you choose by output. The Levoit Large Room lists a 6.2 L tank and 320 ml/h, while the Everlasting Comfort offers 6 L at a lower price but publishes no output.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with humidifiers?
faq.a: Skipping the cleaning. A dirty tank pushes bacteria into the air. Pick a top-fill like the Classic300 or Classic300S and rinse it weekly. Never leave water standing for days.

faq.q: Is the Classic300S worth it over the Classic300?
faq.a: If humidity swings overnight, yes. The Classic300S adds auto mode and smart control, and both sit in the $50 to $100 bracket. If you like a knob and the 60 hour runtime, the Classic300 does the job.

faq.q: How do I set up a humidifier in a bedroom?
faq.a: Place it on a stable, waterproof surface at least a few feet from the bed and walls. Aim the 360 degree nozzle upward, and fill it before sleeping. The Levoit models fill from the top.

faq.q: How often should I clean it?
faq.a: Rinse the tank weekly and descale with white vinegar every couple of weeks if you have hard water. The microbial-resistant tank on the Levoit Large Room slows slime but does not remove the need to clean.

faq.q: Can I add essential oils to the tank?
faq.a: Only if the manufacturer allows it. The unit listed for aromatherapy supports scent, but oils in an ultrasonic tank can leave residue and damage plastics. Use the designated aroma tray if there is one.

finalTake: For most households the Levoit Classic300S is the best humidifier under $150: top fill, auto mode and smart control for $50 to $100. Choose the Levoit Large Room for a big bedroom, the Classic300 for a simple 60 hour runtime, and the Levoit Top Fill when you want the cheapest easy-clean option.
